subject: AI & Agents
title: AI in Video Games
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on AI in Video Games.

hook.text: That enemy NPC just flanked you, took cover, and called for backup. It learned that from watching you.

buildup.text: Game AI uses behavior trees, pathfinding, and sometimes machine learning to create challenge.

discovery.text: Adaptive difficulty AI adjusts the game in real time — harder when you're winning, easier when stuck.

twist.text: Most game AI is scripted to feel intelligent rather than truly being intelligent.

climax.text: New games use AI to generate infinite worlds, dialogues, and quests procedurally.

punchline.text: The best game AI makes you think it's smarter than it is.

quiz.question: How does adaptive difficulty AI work in games?
options: It adjusts challenge level based on the player's performance
It makes the game harder every level

details.summary: AI in video games controls enemy behavior, adapts difficulty, generates content, and creates realistic animations. Game AI ranges from simple rule-based systems to sophisticated machine learning models.
details.whyItMatters: Game AI shapes how fun and challenging your gaming experience is. Understanding it reveals how games create the illusion of intelligent opponents and living worlds.
takeaways: Game AI controls enemy tactics and NPC decision-making
Adaptive difficulty adjusts challenge to match player skill
Procedural content generation creates unique game experiences

faq.question: How does game AI create believable enemy behavior?
faq.answer: Most games use behavior trees and finite state machines that define how enemies react to player actions. Advanced games add randomness and learning to make behavior less predictable.

faq.question: Do games use the same AI as ChatGPT?
faq.answer: Mostly no. Game AI typically uses simpler, faster approaches optimized for real-time performance. Some newer games are experimenting with language models for NPC dialogue, but this is still uncommon.
